Track Markers Down the Resolution Tree to Annotate Clusters

Source: R/Track_markers.R
track_cluster_markers.Rd

Follows the markers found by find_hierarchical_markers() from low to high resolution, to help name clusters. For every gene it shows where it first marks a cluster, how far down that branch it stays detected and where it is lost. For every cluster it suggests a label made of the top marker at each split on the way from the root, e.g. "CST3+ > FCGR3A+", which you translate into a cell type. Labels are suggestions only: you make the final call.

Usage

track_cluster_markers(
  seurat_obj,
  hier = NULL,
  res_cols = NULL,
  pipeline = NULL,
  n_track = 10,
  min_label_auc = 0.8,
  min_global_auc = 0.7,
  n_own = 5,
  sample_name = "Sample",
  output_dir = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

seurat_obj

A Seurat object (the one used for hier).

hier

Optional result of find_hierarchical_markers() on seurat_obj. If NULL (default), it is run with res_cols or pipeline and ....

res_cols, pipeline

Resolution columns or integration method, as in find_hierarchical_markers(). Used only when hier is NULL.

n_track

Integer. Top markers per child and split to track. Default 10.

min_label_auc

Numeric. Minimum AUC against the siblings for a label gene. Default 0.8.

min_global_auc

Numeric. Minimum AUC against all other cells for a gene to be global. Default 0.7.

n_own

Integer. Own markers listed per cluster. Default 5.

sample_name

Character. Used in plot titles and file names. Default "Sample".

output_dir

Character or NULL. If given, the tables (CSV) and plots (JPEG, sized from their content) are saved there. Default NULL.

verbose

Logical. Print progress messages. Default TRUE.

...

Passed to find_hierarchical_markers() when hier is NULL (e.g. assay, min_cells).

Value

A list with:

  • annotation: one row per cluster: node, layer, resolution, cluster, n_cells, is_final, path_label, status ("suggested" / "ambiguous"), reason, confidence (lowest AUC vs siblings of the label genes on the path), min_auc_vs_all (lowest AUC vs all of the label genes), lineage_markers (lineage markers inherited from the splits above), own_markers (top global markers at the cluster's own split), relative_markers (top markers there that are only relative), lowest_purity (on the path).

  • gene_paths: one row per gene and start: gene, start_node, start_resolution, start_split, kind (the marker pattern at the start), auc_at_start, global_at_start, marked_again_below, n_final, n_final_on, final_on, stops_at.

  • node_profile: one row per cluster and tracked gene: node, layer, resolution, gene, mean, pct, pct_rest, log2fc_vs_all, auc_vs_all, global, auc_vs_siblings, is_marker.

  • plots: tree (tree with the label gene of every split), heatmap (AUC against all cells of the tracked genes at every cluster, markers dotted) and dotplot (label genes across the final clusters in tree order).

  • hier: the find_hierarchical_markers() result used.

  • parameters.

Details

Tracked genes. The top n_track markers (by AUC against the siblings) of every child at every split.

Profile. For each tracked gene at every cluster of every resolution: mean expression, share of cells detected (pct) and outside the cluster (pct_rest), log2 fold change and AUC against all other cells, and AUC against its siblings (the other children of its parent; all their cells). global is auc_vs_all >= min_global_auc: the gene is high in the cluster compared with the whole object, not only compared with its siblings ("relative").

Gene paths. A gene's path starts at a cluster where it is a marker and no cluster above it on the branch is marked by it. Below the start, a cluster is "on" when the gene is detected in at least min_pct of its cells (the detection filter of find_hierarchical_markers()); stops_at lists the first clusters where it is no longer on.

Labels. For each split on the way from the root, the label gene is the highest-ranked global marker among the top n_track of that child (if none is global, the top marker, flagged relative). A label is "ambiguous" when, at any split on its path, there is no marker (or the child was too small to test), the label gene's AUC against the siblings is below min_label_auc, the label gene is only relative, it is lower in the cluster than in the rest of the object (AUC against all < 0.5), or a cluster on the path has low purity. reason says which.

Statistics use the same cells and clusters, so they describe the data rather than prove the labels; check the labels against known biology.

See also

find_hierarchical_markers()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
hier <- find_hierarchical_markers(my_seurat, pipeline = "log.rpca")
ann <- track_cluster_markers(my_seurat, hier = hier, output_dir = "Track_markers")
ann$annotation[, c("node", "path_label", "status", "reason")]
subset(ann$gene_paths, gene == "GZMK")
ann$plots$heatmap
} # }
